selection: Natural terminal lakes that ADR-112 permits as a separate water type: a closed basin with no dam and no engineered full pool, an owner-operated daily series of surface elevation with its vertical datum, a volume only where the survey publishes one daily on a published elevation-volume relation (an entry without one states why in no_volume, ADR-161), and a reviewed waterbody point that resolves to exactly one NHDPlus HR waterbody at the project's 100-metre tolerance. A lake whose parts the survey measures apart is one entry per measured arm, each keyed by its own station and naming its arm; the entries share the lake's name and are published as one lake with its arms kept apart, never as one combined level or volume (ADR-112, ADR-161). No capacity, percent full, dam point or reservoir-rollup membership is recorded for any lake here, and a restoration or regulatory level is only ever a named target with its authority and date. Walker Lake was the first admission and Great Salt Lake the second; the candidates still held are in the withheld block with their findings.

point.source: USGS monitoring location USGS-10288500, WALKER LAKE NR HAWTHORNE, NV, in decimal degrees on NAD83 (the site record's coordinate datum is NAD27; the decimal coordinates are the survey's NAD83 conversion)

waterbody.note: The site point resolves to exactly one NHDPlus HR waterbody within 100 metres, and Esri's USA Detailed Water Bodies names the same lake -- the probe's strongest outcome (ADR-106). The point is a gauge on the shore and stands for the whole lake; no outlet or dam point exists to record.

closed_basin.evidence: The Walker River ends in the lake and water leaves the basin by evaporation; the lake has no outlet (Lopes and Smith, 2007, SIR 2007-5012). The committed west-huc8 geometry places the site point in subbasin 16050304 Walker Lake inside basin 160503 Walker, and the survey's own hydrologic unit for the site agrees. The assignment is made from the published lake point, never from a synthetic outlet (ADR-112).

elevation.note: Reservoir elevation, the daily observation at 24:00, in feet above the site's vertical datum. The survey records the datum as NGVD29 with a site altitude of 3,900 feet. An elevation is published as a level and never as a percentage of any datum (ADR-112).

relation.name: Lopes and Smith (2007), Bathymetry of Walker Lake, West-Central Nevada, U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2007-5012
relation.note: The survey computes storage from the lake stage with this relation from 1 October 2014; the relation used before that date was Rush (1970). Recorded from ADR-112's review of 2026-09-04; the water-year summaries that state the change were not reachable on 2026-09-06. The published record starts on 2015-01-01, inside the current relation, so every published volume is on one relation and no reading is recomputed or repaired.

10010000.name: Great Salt Lake

arm.name: South arm
arm.evidence: The survey's Utah Water Science Center names station 10010000, at Saltair Boat Harbor at the southern end of the lake, for the south part, and station 10010100, northwest of Saline, for the north part, monitored since April 1966. "The Union Pacific Railroad causeway completed in 1959, essentially divides the lake into two parts", and the south part's surface is usually higher because most of the inflow enters it. The site point is south of the causeway.

point.source: USGS monitoring location USGS-10010000, GREAT SALT LAKE AT SALTAIR BOAT HARBOR, UT, in decimal degrees on NAD83 (the site record's original coordinate datum is NAD27), located by GPS and accurate to plus or minus one second

waterbody.note: The site point resolves to exactly one NHDPlus HR waterbody within 100 metres, and Esri's USA Detailed Water Bodies names the same lake -- the probe's strongest outcome (ADR-106). Both arms' points resolve to this one polygon: the hydrography maps Great Salt Lake as one water body and does not divide it at the causeway, so the arms are told apart by their stations and never by a polygon (ADR-161).

closed_basin.evidence: The survey describes Great Salt Lake as "a terminal lake with no outlet to the sea" (https://www.usgs.gov/centers/utah-water-science-center/science/great-salt-lake-elevations-and-areal-extent). The committed west-huc8 geometry places the Saltair Boat Harbor site point in subbasin 16020310 Great Salt Lake inside basin 160203 Great Salt Lake, and the survey's own hydrologic unit for the site agrees. The assignment is made from the published site point, never from a synthetic outlet (ADR-112).

datum_review.note: The datum is part of the series' own definition: the survey defines parameter 62614 as lake or reservoir elevation above NGVD29 (the code 62615 is the NAVD88 series, and 00062 states no datum). The site record's vertical datum agrees. This is the measuring agency's own series and not a republication, so the agreement ADR-139 asks of a Reclamation level is not the test here; no conversion is applied and the level is published as the survey writes it (ADR-161).

elevation.note: Lake elevation, the daily mean, in feet above NGVD29. The survey's daily series begins on 1847-10-18; the published record starts on 2015-01-01, the project's shared start. An elevation is published as a level and never as a percentage of any datum (ADR-112).

10010000.no_volume: The survey publishes no daily volume for this arm: its time-series metadata for the station lists the lake elevation (62614) and nothing else. A volume computed here from a published table would be this project's figure and not the survey's, and no combined volume for the two arms is published either, so the record carries the level alone (ADR-161).

withheld.Pyramid Lake: ADR-112's second candidate. The survey publishes a strong elevation series and no reviewed modern volume relation in this project. ADR-161 made the volume block optional, so the missing volume no longer holds it; what holds it now is that its station identity, vertical datum, waterbody point and closed-basin assignment have not been reviewed. Held until those reviews are recorded here.
withheld.Mono Lake: Its regulatory restoration level is a target set by the California State Water Resources Control Board and not a physical capacity (ADR-112). A target may be published only as a named target with its authority and date; held until the measurement series and the target's citation are reviewed together.
